**What happened**:
The [following](https://host-586.example//view/gs/proj-prow/pr-logs/pull/proj_proj/64673/job-7129/5645537119207273897) CI failure of 
```
[test_id:95944] Should force restart a VM with terminationGracePeriodSeconds>0
```
Revealed a real bug. VM force restart is performed by the virt-api and it includes two steps:
1. Sending PATCH to VM status `stateChangeRequests` with `Stop` and `Start`
2. Sending DELETE call to the VMI pod with grace period of 1 second

The race condition happens between step 1 and 2, The VM conttoller reconciles the VM state and stops the VMI, the VMI controller in turn reconciles the VMI and deletes the VMI pod. 
Because of the [following](https://host-623.example/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/93928) kubelet limitation, the `StopContainer` action performed by kubelet and CRI-O is blocking. It means that if the VMI controller fires the pod deletion before virt-api, the grace period of 1 second isn't being honored during the delete call from virt-api. 

In the test scenario the `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` is being set with 600 seconds. From the k8s-reporter artifacts it can be seen that the pod `virt-launcher-testvmi-2pgv4-jfl5b` of the VM `testvmi-2pgv4`
is stuck in `Terminating` phase, causing the test to fail. Pod metadata has `deletionGracePeriodSeconds` label set to `1` which means that pod deletion with grace period 1 indeed received by the k8s API server. 
But from the k8s events log it is seen that:
```

                "name": "testvmi-2pgv4.18a1c686e77df28d",

``` 
It means that VMI controller also sent the pod delete command. By looking at CRIO logs it is seen that:
```
Mar 30 20:46:51 node02 crio[892]: time="2026-03-30T20:46:51.522836982-04:00" level=info msg="Stopping container: 823dcef5b41865126d1591d8edc18d7e403965c3e4d071c8b2a19e05bd1645bb (timeout: 630s)" id=b5a351a6-b788-4044-9127-bd33ce0f8e75 name=/runtime.v1.RuntimeService/StopContainer

```
The `(timeout: 630s)` indicates that `StopContainer` was sent with the 600 seconds defined in the test and not with the 1 second that was probably received later.

**What you expected to happen**:
Respecting the single writer principle. I would expect the VMI controller to send the pod delete with the relevant grace period.

{"author": "person-85748ec1", "body": "# What happened

Flaky test detected: `[cbt] runOverlayQMPSession should send dismiss and quit only after concluded` [1]

/kind flake
/sig storage

[1]: https://host-586.example/view/gs/proj-prow/pr-logs/pull/proj_proj/62839/job-6610/2004124431316202874

## Additional context

`runOverlayQMPSession` in `pkg/component-547/virtwrap/storage/cbt.go` uses a `select` on three channels: `concludedChan`, `scanDone`, and `ctx.Done()`. When the scanner goroutine reads from an in-memory `strings.NewReader` (as in the unit test), it finds the `concluded` event and closes `concludedChan`, then immediately hits EOF and closes `scanDone`. Both channels become ready at essentially the same time.

Go's `select` picks a random ready case when multiple are available, so it non-deterministically chooses `scanDone` over `concludedChan`, causing the spurious error:

```
qemu-storage-daemon exited without job concluding for overlay /test/overlay.qcow2
```

### CI search results

Searching for `exited without job concluding` over the last 14 days found **3 matches** in `job-6610` out of 445 total runs, accounting for ~5% of the 61 failed runs in that job.

### Fix

The fix adds a nested non-blocking check on `concludedChan` inside the `scanDone` case, giving it priority — the standard Go idiom for channel priority in a `select`:

```go
case <-scanDone:
    select {
    case <-concludedChan:
        fmt.Fprintf(stdin, "%s\n%s\n%s\n", queryJobs, jobDismiss, quit)
    default:
        err = fmt.Errorf("qemu-storage-daemon exited without job concluding for overlay %s", overlayPath)
    }
```

# Flake Action Plan

### The flake is a bug

The fix is straightforward — a one-line change to add priority channel selection. A PR will follow referencing this issue.", "closed_by": null, "comments": [{"author": "person-85748ec1", "body": "## Example failing job URLs

{"author": "person-85748ec1", "body": "# What happened

The `job-8695` job failed with two timeout-related flakes on PR #82938:

Flaky tests detected:
1. `DomainNotifyServer integration [It] should be resilient to notify server restarts`
2. `AccessCredentials [It] should support multiple ssh keys in one secret value`

Failing job: https://host-586.example/view/gs/proj-prow/pr-logs/pull/proj_proj/82938/job-8695/3242341301257321333

/kind flake

## Failure Details

### 1. DomainNotifyServer - should be resilient to notify server restarts

**File:** `pkg/component-261/launcher-clients/launcher-clients_test.go:220`

```
[FAILED] Unexpected error: context deadline exceeded
```

The test repeatedly restarts a notify server and expects the client to reconnect within tight timeouts (1s connect, 3s overall). On arm64, the reconnection loop hits `connect: no such file or directory` errors while the server is restarting, and the `context deadline exceeded` before a successful connection can be made.

This is a recurrence of #47123 which was previously closed as rotten.

### 2. AccessCredentials - should support multiple ssh keys in one secret value

**File:** `pkg/component-547/virtwrap/access-credentials/access_credentials_test.go:281`

```
[FAILED] Timed out after 5.000s. Expected <chan struct {} | len:0, cap:0> to be closed
```

The test waits for an `Eventually` with a 5-second timeout for a channel to be closed after SSH key propagation. On arm64, the mock-based credential handling does not complete within this window.

## Root Cause

Both failures are caused by timeouts that are too tight for the arm64 CI environment. The arm64 unit test job likely runs under emulation or on constrained hardware, making these timing-sensitive tests unreliable.

## Additional context

- PR #82938 is unrelated to both test areas (it quarantines a sig-scale test), confirming these are pre-existing flakes.
- The DomainNotifyServer flake was previously reported as #47123 and closed as rotten without a fix.

This looks like a gap in how KinD providers set up storage for CDI. The root cause is that CDI's StorageProfile auto-detection doesn't properly populate `accessModes` for the `rancher.io/local-path` provisioner used by KinD, while on the regular K8s provider the `host-860.example/no-provisioner` with the local-volume-provisioner DaemonSet works correctly [[1]](https://host-623.example/proj/projci/blob/b6dd83e8a72aeb3fdf20f4633cc2f1c7e77ec4ca/cluster-up/cluster/kind/manifests/local-storage-class.yaml) [[2]](https://host-623.example/proj/projci/blob/b6dd83e8a72aeb3fdf20f4633cc2f1c7e77ec4ca/cluster-provision/k8s/1.33/manifests/local-volume.yaml).

When CDI deploys on a KinD cluster, it creates a StorageProfile for the `local` StorageClass but fails to populate its `claimPropertySets` with `accessModes`, leading to the `no accessMode specified in StorageProfile local` error when DataVolumes are created [[3]](https://host-623.example/proj/proj/blob/84ff809176232d94d4f3ae90edab4e6a8a96ace3/pkg/component-328/types/cdi.go#L39-L41).

There's prior work in projci that explicitly added the `local` StorageClass manifest for KinD [[4]](https://host-623.example/proj/projci/pull/85461), but no equivalent step creates or patches the StorageProfile with the required `accessModes`. A similar approach could fix this — adding an explicit StorageProfile manifest to the KinD cluster-up scripts [[5]](https://host-623.example/proj/projci/blob/b6dd83e8a72aeb3fdf20f4633cc2f1c7e77ec4ca/cluster-up/cluster/kind/common.sh#L267-L271).

**Immediate workaround**: After `make cluster-up` and CDI deployment, patch the StorageProfile:

```yaml
apiVersion: cdi.proj.example/v1beta1
kind: StorageProfile
metadata:
  name: local
spec:
  claimPropertySets:
  - accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
    volumeMode: Filesystem
```

**Long-term fix**: The KinD provider's cluster-up scripts in projci should be updated to create/patch the `local` StorageProfile with appropriate `claimPropertySets` after CDI is deployed, similar to how the `local` StorageClass manifest was explicitly added in [projci PR #85461](https://host-623.example/proj/projci/pull/85461) [[6]](https://host-623.example/proj/projci/pull/85461).

You can verify the current state with:

```bash
kubectl get storageprofile local -o jsonpath='{.status.claimPropertySets}'
```

If this returns empty/null, that confirms the issue.

{"author": "person-bf91c6e0", "body": "## Summary

The `virt-exportproxy` pod in the `proj` namespace panics and enters **CrashLoopBackOff**, causing 24 cascading serial test failures in `job-9845`.

## Failing Job

- **Job**: [job-9845 / 3059281404328236697](https://host-586.example/view/gs/proj-prow/logs/job-9845/3059281404328236697)
- **Date**: 2026-04-24
- **Result**: 517 Passed | 26 Failed | 4 Pending | 833 Skipped (suite timeout elapsed)

## Root Cause

The `virt-exportproxy` container panics early in the test run. The build log detects:

```
ERROR: Found panic in test output
Files:
/logs/artifacts/k8s-reporter/1/pods/2_proj_virt-exportproxy-6cd5b869cd-8qvrw-exportproxy.log
/logs/artifacts/k8s-reporter/1/pods/2_proj_virt-exportproxy-6cd5b869cd-8qvrw-exportproxy_previous.log
```

The restart count escalates throughout the run:

| Snapshot | Restarts | BackOff Events |
|---|---|---|
| process=1/failure=2 | 9 | 27 |
| process=1/failure=3 | 11 | 33 |
| process=1/failure=5 | 15 | 59 |
| suite/failure=0 | **35** | **99974** |

## Cascading Failures

All 24 serial test failures share the same pattern — they fail in `[AfterEach]` at `tests/component-779/fixture.go:44920` with:

```
Timed out after 300.000s.
One of the Proj control-plane components is not ready.
Expected condition of type 'Available' and status 'True' but got 'False'
```

2. Determine if this is a new regression or a known flake
3. Consider whether the AfterEach timeout (300s) is sufficient given a crashing component, or if the test framework should detect CrashLoopBackOff earlier and skip remaining serial tests

{"author": "person-bf91c6e0", "body": "## Summary

The test `[sig-storage] Volumes update with migration Hotplug volumes should be able to volume migrate a VM with a datavolume and an hotplugged datavolume migrating from block to filesystem` is failing at a ~21% rate on k8s 1.36, while it is stable (0% failure) on k8s 1.34 and 1.35.

## Failure Rate (from testgrid)

| Lane (k8s version) | Failure Rate | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **k8s 1.36** sig-storage | **21.4% (12/56 runs)** | Flaky |
| **k8s 1.35** sig-storage | **0.0% (0/225 runs)** | Stable |
| **k8s 1.34** sig-storage | **0.0% (0/42409 runs)** | Stable |

### Related test variants on k8s 1.36

| Migration direction | Failure Rate |
|---|---|
| block → filesystem | **21.4%** (worst) |
| filesystem → filesystem | **8.9%** |
| block → block | 0% |
| filesystem → block | 0% |

Pattern: migrations **targeting filesystem** volumes are affected on k8s 1.36 only. Migrations targeting block storage are stable.

## Root Cause (from build 3309147724183903808)

The destination PVC ends up with **0 bytes** allocated, causing QEMU to fail immediately:

```
Volume migration cannot be performed because the destination volume is smaller than the source volume:
virError(Code=1, Domain=10, Message='internal error: process exited while connecting to monitor:
qemu-kvm: -blockdev {"driver":"raw","file":"libvirt-1-storage","offset":0,"size":1000341504,
"node-name":"libvirt-1-slice-sto","read-only":false,"discard":"unmap","cache":{"direct":true,
"no-flush":false}}: The sum of offset (0) and size (1000341504) has to be smaller or equal to
the actual size of the containing file (0)')
```

K8s cluster events from the failing run show:
- **ClaimMisbound**: two claims bound to the same PV
- **ProvisioningFailed**: conflict error saving the PVC
- **FailedScheduling**: importer pod has unbound immediate PVCs
- 25x **MigrationBackoff** followed by 360s timeout

This suggests a PVC provisioning/binding race condition that is specific to k8s 1.36.

{"author": "person-bf91c6e0", "body": "## Summary

Two non-quarantined hotplug volume migration tests are failing at high rates in `job-1952` over the last 14 days (56 builds, Apr 29 – May 13 2026).

## Affected Tests

| Test | Success Rate | Failed / Total Runs |
|------|-------------|---------------------|
| `[sig-storage] Volumes update with migration Hotplug volumes should be able to volume migrate a VM with a datavolume and an hotplugged datavolume migrating from block to filesystem` | **61.1%** | 21 / 54 |
| `[sig-storage] Volumes update with migration Hotplug volumes should be able to volume migrate a VM with a datavolume and an hotplugged datavolume migrating from filesystem to filesystem` | **79.6%** | 11 / 54 |

## Failure Pattern

Both tests fail with the same timeout pattern — 360s timeout waiting for volume migration to complete:

```
tests/storage/migration.go:1275
Timed out after 360.000s.
Expected
   ...cted
       <bool>: true
   to be false
}

tests/storage/migration.go:1382
```

Failures occur almost daily (block→fs) or every other day (fs→fs), and are not correlated with specific builds or infrastructure events.

## Cross-Version Comparison (k8s 1.34 / 1.35 / 1.36)

Comparing the `job-2814{version}-sig-storage` lanes over the same 14-day window:

### Hotplug volume migration tests — **1.36-specific regression**

| Test | k8s 1.34 | k8s 1.35 | k8s 1.36 |
|------|----------|----------|----------|
| block → filesystem | **0 failures** | **0 failures** | **21 / 54 (61.1%)** |
| filesystem → filesystem | **0 failures** | **0 failures** | **11 / 54 (79.6%)** |
| containerdisk + hotplugged volume | **0 failures** | **0 failures** | **1 / 54 (98.1%)** |

Both hotplug volume migration tests pass 100% on k8s 1.34 and 1.35. All failures are isolated to k8s 1.36, pointing to a **k8s 1.36 behavioral change or incompatibility** affecting volume migration rather than a general Proj flake.

### Quarantined tests — consistent across versions

| Test | k8s 1.34 | k8s 1.35 | k8s 1.36 |
|------|----------|----------|----------|
| `[QUARANTINE] should pause VMI on IO error` | 34/54 (37.0%) | 34/54 (37.0%) | 27/54 (50.0%) |
| `[QUARANTINE] cancel migration delete source migration` | 1/54 (98.1%) | 6/54 (88.9%) | 3/54 (94.4%) |

These are known flakes, already quarantined, and not version-specific.

### Lane health overview

|------|--------|-------------------|
| k8s **1.34** | 55 | 2 (both quarantined) |
| k8s **1.35** | 56 | 3 (2 quarantined + 1 one-off) |
| k8s **1.36** | 56 | 6 (2 quarantined + 2 regressions + 2 one-offs) |

{"author": "person-bf91c6e0", "body": "## Summary

The test `[sig-compute] VM state with persistent TPM VM option enabled should persist VM state of TPM across migration and restart` fails intermittently due to a race condition between source domain cleanup and migration status finalization.

The migration **succeeds at the QEMU/libvirt level** but the API-level `VirtualMachineInstanceMigration` object is never updated to "Succeeded", causing the test to time out after 240s.

## Observed in

- **Build**: [job-6409 / 5730344574365621131](https://host-586.example/view/gs/proj-prow/pr-logs/pull/batch/job-6409/5730344574365621131)
- **Batch PRs** (neither PR is related to the failure):
  - #50488 — Graduate DeclarativeHotplugVolumes to Beta
  - #48274 — VEP183: Add DRA-backed network devices (alpha)

## Timeline

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 09:52:55 | Test starts migration |
| 09:52:58 | virt-controller hands off migration `test-migration-98x9m` to target virt-handler |
| 09:52:59 | Target domain appears (`Paused/StartingUp`) |
| 09:53:01 | Block migration data transfer completes (~265MB across 8 parallel threads in ~3s) |
| 09:53:01.613 | Source domain: `Shutoff/Migrated`, Target domain: `Running` — **migration succeeded** |
| 09:53:01.614 | Source virt-handler VM controller immediately signals deletion and starts local cleanup |
| 09:53:01–09:53:04 | migration-source controller still sees `VMI phase: Running` but source domain is already gone |
| 09:53:04–09:56:55 | **4-minute gap** — no further processing of this migration on the source |
| 09:56:55 | **Test times out**: `migration is in the phase: Running` |
| 09:56:59 | virt-controller finally triggers migration recovery — **too late** |

## Root Cause

The source virt-handler's VM controller sees `Shutoff/Migrated`, races ahead with cleanup/deletion, and destroys the local domain before the migration-source controller can finalize the migration status. The migration object gets stuck in "Running" state. The virt-controller's recovery mechanism (which checks for orphaned migrations) only kicks in ~4 minutes later — after the 240s test timeout has already fired.

## Evidence from Container Logs

**virt-controller** (`virt-controller-85fdfc7b9f-nqbrl`):
- 09:52:58 — `Handed off migration proj-test-default2/test-migration-98x9m to target virt-handler`
- 09:56:59 — `reenqueuing Migration ... reason: a migration recovery had to be initiated` (4 min gap)

**Source virt-handler** (`virt-handler-z5djk`):
- 09:53:01.614 — `Signaled deletion for testvmi-gs4gg-*`
- 09:53:01.616 — `Performing final local cleanup for vmi with uid b856ff05-ead2-4ebc-832c-983fe132ef52`
- 09:53:01.617 — migration-source still reports `VMI is in phase: Running` while domain is already gone
- 09:53:04 — Last migration-source log entry; no further processing until test timeout

**Target virt-handler** (`virt-handler-p4cks`):
- 09:53:01.380 — `Domain is in state Running reason Unknown` — migration completed successfully on target

## Additional Context

- The test is tagged with `[no-flake-check]`, indicating known flaky behavior
- No infrastructure issues in this build: no CrashLoopBackOff, no NotReady nodes, no etcd problems
- 460 of 73880 tests passed
- This is a block migration (disk0 + cloudinitdisk volumes)

{"author": "person-85748ec1", "base": "main", "body": "### What this PR does
#### Before this PR:

Proj uses hardcoded SPDY dialers and executors for port-forwarding
and remote exec in 4 call sites. Since Kubernetes 1.31, the
`PortForwardWebsockets` feature gate has been beta (on by default),
meaning the API server handles port-forward connections through its
WebSocket infrastructure. In k8s 1.35 this graduates to GA (locked on).

When Proj sends a pure SPDY upgrade request to an API server with
WebSocket port-forwarding enabled, the upgrade is accepted but SPDY
stream creation within the connection is unreliable. This causes
intermittent failures in CI:

- **k8s 1.35**: 148 build-log matches for `error creating forwarding
  stream` across 549 runs (25% of runs affected)
- **k8s 1.34**: 38 build-log matches across 84331 runs (26% of runs
  affected)

#### Example CI failure

From
[job-7504/9147014309318307853](https://host-586.example/view/gs/proj-prow/pr-logs/pull/batch/job-7504/9147014309318307853):

```
portforward.go:380] "Unhandled Error" err="error creating forwarding stream for port 8443 -> 8443: EOF"
portforward.go:380] "Unhandled Error" err="error creating forwarding stream for port 8444 -> 8443: EOF"
portforward.go:380] "Unhandled Error" err="error creating forwarding stream for port 8440 -> 8443: Timeout occurred"
portforward.go:380] "Unhandled Error" err="error creating forwarding stream for port 8441 -> 8443: Timeout occurred"
portforward.go:357] "Unhandled Error" err="error creating error stream for port 8442 -> 8443: Timeout occurred"
portforward.go:357] "Unhandled Error" err="error creating error stream for port 8445 -> 8443: Timeout occurred"
```

These SPDY stream failures break the pod-level port-forward tunnels
used by tests to fetch TLS certificates and execute commands inside
pods.

#### What this PR fixes (and what it doesn't)

The SPDY port-forward code we're fixing is used for **pod-level
operations**:

- `ForwardPorts()` in `tests/component-932/certs.go` forwards to individual
  Proj pods (virt-api, virt-handler) on port 8443 to fetch TLS
  certificates
- `ExecuteCommandOnPodWithOptions()` in `tests/component-957/execute.go` runs
  commands inside pods

Both go through the Kubernetes pod portforward/exec API endpoints,
which is where the SPDY-to-WebSocket upgrade path causes the stream
creation failures shown above.

Note: the `TLS handshake timeout` errors that also appear in these
failing runs (e.g. `Get "https://127.0.0.1:43619/api/v1/nodes":
net/http: TLS handshake timeout`) are on the **kube-apiserver port**.
The projci test infrastructure accesses the kube-apiserver through
a **podman container port mapping** (`--random-ports` maps container
port 6443 to a random localhost port), not through kubectl
port-forward or SPDY. This can be seen in the [build log](https://host-751.example/proj-prow/pr-logs/pull/batch/job-7504/9147014309318307853/build-log.txt)
at line 901:
```
_kubectl config set-cluster kubernetes --server=https://127.0.0.1:43619
```
These TLS handshake timeouts may be a separate issue and this PR does
not claim to fix them.

#### The servers are healthy during the SPDY stream failures

From the [same failing run's build log](https://host-751.example/proj-prow/pr-logs/pull/batch/job-7504/9147014309318307853/build-log.txt),
all Proj components are `1/1 Running` at deploy time (17:32), and
the kube-apiserver passes its health check at 17:24:

```
NAME                               READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
virt-api-67494ff85d-h664m          1/1     Running   0          59s
virt-api-67494ff85d-hvfgw          1/1     Running   0          59s
virt-controller-6bdd6d8869-97dz9   1/1     Running   0          34s
virt-controller-6bdd6d8869-qwlks   1/1     Running   0          34s
virt-handler-xp9h7                 1/1     Running   0          34s
virt-handler-zlmrq                 1/1     Running   0          34s
```

Tests continue to pass (`•`) right alongside the portforward errors,
confirming the servers are serving requests when the port-forward
tunnel happens to work:
```
18:27:00: •SSSS...•••••••S•SSSSSSE0225 18:27:00 portforward.go:380]
          "error creating forwarding stream for port 8443 -> 8443: EOF"
18:27:15: •SS          <-- tests still passing
18:27:30: SSE0225 18:27:30 portforward.go:380]
          "error creating forwarding stream for port 8440 -> 8443: Timeout occurred"
18:30:02: ••SSSSSSS    <-- tests still passing
```

In this run, **62 of 147 tests pass**. The failures are confined to
tests that need pod-level port-forwarding or exec during the window
when SPDY stream creation fails.

#### Why it's intermittent

The failures are timing-dependent, not all-or-nothing:

1. The initial SPDY upgrade is **accepted** by the API server, so the
   connection appears to succeed
2. But the API server internally routes through its WebSocket
   port-forward path, creating a protocol impedance mismatch
3. Individual SPDY streams (data + error streams, one pair per
   forwarded port) are created **after** the connection is established
4. Whether each stream creation races with connection lifecycle events
   depends on timing and load
5. Some streams may succeed while others fail in the same connection
   (e.g. ports 8443-8444 get EOF, ports 8440-8442 timeout)
6. The `EventuallyWithOffset` retry loop in test helpers can mask some
   failures, so not every stream error causes a test failure

#### After this PR:

All 4 SPDY usage sites are migrated to use WebSocket as the primary
transport with SPDY as a fallback, using the vendored `client-go`
fallback wrappers:

- `tests/component-932/certs.go` (`ForwardPorts`):
  `portforward.NewFallbackDialer`
- `tests/component-957/execute.go` (`ExecuteCommandOnPodWithOptions`):
  `remotecommand.NewFallbackExecutor`
- `pkg/component-264/vmexport/vmexport.go` (`RunPortForward`):
  `portforward.NewFallbackDialer`
- `pkg/component-264/guestfs/guestfs.go` (`CreateAttacher`):
  `remotecommand.NewFallbackExecutor`

With WebSocket as the primary transport, both client and server speak
the same protocol natively — no SPDY-over-WebSocket tunneling, no
protocol impedance mismatch, no stream creation failures.

The fallback uses `httpstream.IsUpgradeFailure` to detect when the
WebSocket upgrade is not supported and transparently falls back to
SPDY for older API servers.

### References

- https://host-623.example/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/85021 (PortForwardWebsockets GA in k8s 1.35)
- [CI search: `error creating forwarding stream` on k8s 1.35](https://host-498.example/?search=error+creating+forwarding+stream&name=job-7504%24&type=build-log&maxAge=336h)

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The vendored `client-go` already provides
`portforward.NewSPDYOverWebsocketDialer`,
`portforward.NewFallbackDialer`, `remotecommand.NewWebSocketExecutor`,
and `remotecommand.NewFallbackExecutor`. These are the same APIs that
upstream Kubernetes tooling (e.g. `kubectl port-forward`, `kubectl
exec`) uses for the WebSocket transition. Wrapping both transports with
the fallback pattern ensures:

- **k8s 1.31+** (WebSocket enabled): WebSocket (primary) succeeds
  immediately, eliminating the protocol mismatch
- **Older k8s**: WebSocket upgrade fails,
  `httpstream.IsUpgradeFailure` triggers transparent fallback to SPDY

No new dependencies are introduced — all APIs are already vendored.

### Special notes for your reviewer

The pattern applied is identical across all 4 sites: create the SPDY
dialer/executor, create the WebSocket dialer/executor, wrap with the
fallback. This mirrors what `kubectl` itself does internally.

{"author": "person-85748ec1", "base": "main", "body": "### What this PR does
#### Before this PR:

Proj hardcodes OVMF firmware paths (e.g. `OVMF_CODE.secboot.fd`,
`OVMF_VARS.secboot.fd`) and constructs explicit `<loader>` / `<nvram>` paths
in the domain XML for EFI Secure Boot.

#### After this PR:

For standard EFI Secure Boot (not SEV/SNP/TDX), Proj uses libvirt's
firmware auto-selection feature (`<os firmware='efi'>` with
`<firmware><feature>` elements), delegating loader selection to libvirt
based on JSON descriptor files shipped by the `edk2-ovmf` package.

The NVRAM path continues to be explicitly set by Proj via
`PathForNVram()` with `format='raw'` to preserve the existing filename
convention (`<vmi.Name>_VARS.fd`), ensure compatibility with persistent
EFI backend storage mounts, and prevent NVRAM corruption if firmware
descriptors prefer qcow2 format. Full NVRAM delegation to libvirt is
planned for beta (see VEP).

This is guarded by a new `FirmwareAutoSelection` feature gate (Alpha,
default disabled). The feature gate is passed to virt-launcher via a
`--firmware-auto-selection` CLI flag set by virt-controller, following
the established pattern used by `--libvirt-hook-server-and-client` and
`--upgrade-ordinal-ifaces`.

### References

- VEP tracking issue: https://host-623.example/proj/enhancements/issues/85938
- VEP PR: https://host-623.example/proj/enhancements/pull/90959

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

See [VEP #85938](https://host-623.example/proj/enhancements/pull/90959) for full
motivation. In short: eliminates fragile hardcoded firmware paths, delegates
firmware selection to libvirt, and unifies the approach with ARM64 Secure Boot
([VEP #42409](https://host-623.example/proj/enhancements/issues/42409)).

The following tradeoffs were made:
- Only standard Secure Boot uses auto-selection. SEV/SNP/TDX and non-SB EFI
  continue using explicit paths due to missing firmware descriptors and
  fallback logic concerns (detailed in VEP).
- Guarded by a feature gate despite being an internal change, to provide a
  safety net for NVRAM path handling differences during initial rollout.
- NVRAM path is kept explicit during alpha to avoid a filename convention
  mismatch between Proj (`<vmi.Name>_VARS.fd`) and libvirt's domain name
  (`<namespace>_<vmi-name>_VARS.fd`) that would silently reset EFI state.
  Full NVRAM delegation is planned for beta with proper migration.
- `format='raw'` is set on the `<nvram>` element to prevent NVRAM corruption
  if the auto-selected firmware descriptor prefers qcow2 format.
- Feature gate is passed via CLI flag rather than protobuf to avoid
  permanently polluting the gRPC schema with a field that will be removed
  at GA.

The following alternatives were considered:
- Keep explicit paths (fragile, duplicates libvirt logic)
- Auto-selection for all EFI modes (higher risk, blocked by missing descriptors)
- No feature gate (rejected — NVRAM path handling warrants a safety net)
- Protobuf field for feature gate (rejected — CLI flag is the established
  pattern and avoids permanent gRPC schema pollution)

### Special notes for your reviewer

- The `<nvram>` element uses `format='raw'` to guard against NVRAM format
  mismatch on upgrade (per libvirt maintainer feedback on the VEP).
- Tests cover amd64 and arm64 EFI paths via `DescribeTable` with explicit
  `efiEnvironment` overrides to ensure arch-specific coverage regardless
  of host architecture.

{"author": "person-4f4debd1", "base": "main", "body": "### What this PR does
#### Before this PR:
- Bridge Services tests used a Cirros VMI and LoginToCirros which is not supported on s390x.
- After WaitUntilVMIReady, the test started vmnetserver right away—no wait for eth0 / DHCP / IPv4.
- createServiceConnectivityJob always used \<name\>.\<namespace\> as the client target so DNS may not resolve, and the test times out even when the Service and VMI are fine. 
- The headless / pod DNS case targeted hostname.subdomain only, not a full *.svc.cluster.local name.
- vmnetserver TCP used nc with a bare printf “Hello World!” path, so BusyBox nc could close before the job read the response.

#### After this PR:
- Bridge Services tests use an Alpine VMI and LoginToAlpine.
- waitForAlpinePodNetworkIPv4 runs after login: bring up eth0, run udhcpc, then wait until eth0 has an IPv4 (login can finish before the pod network is ready).
- createServiceConnectivityJob picks the target host as: Service ClusterIP when the name matches a Service with a real ClusterIP; if Get fails and the name contains dots, treat it as a full FQDN; otherwise name.namespace (so invalid service names still behave as before).
- The headless test uses hostname.subdomain.namespace.svc.cluster.local.
- vmnetserver TCP uses sh -c with printf 'Hello World!'; sleep 2 so the hello-world Job can read the line reliably.

{"author": "person-4c34b631", "base": "main", "body": "### What this PR does

Cleanup and hardening of the source-side live migration monitor, abort flow, and cross-component error handling. Built on top of #60112 and #71803.

#### Migration monitor simplification
- Remove `determineNonRunningMigrationStatus` and `completedJobInfo` caching — all code paths already covered by `MigrateToURI3` error return and `migrationErrorChan`
- Remove `migrationFailedWithError` two-phase error handling — errors processed immediately
- Remove redundant `DOMAIN_JOB_CANCELLED` handling — always followed by `MigrateToURI3` error
- Retrieve completed migration stats via libvirt job completion event instead of polling
- Fix monitor busy loop after successful migration (fallback `GetJobStats` with `COMPLETED` flag)
- Log actual Downtime/DowntimeNet for completed jobs
- Move volume size error rewrite into `setMigrationResultHelper` where it runs on first call

#### Migration abort decoupling
- Delegate all abort calls from monitor to `cancelMigration()` — single guarded path with `AbortStatus` tracking
- Separate `setMigrationAbortStatus` from `setMigrationResult` — abort only sets abort, result only sets result
- `asyncMigrationAbort` no longer calls `setMigrationResult` directly
- Add `sync.WaitGroup` so `migrateHelper` waits for in-flight abort before `migrate()` sets final result
- `migrate()` is now the sole owner of `setMigrationResult` on all paths

#### Monitor reliability
- Gate migration start on monitor readiness — if monitor can't initialize, migration doesn't proceed
- Replace `migrationErrorChan` (bidirectional `chan error`) with `migrationDone` (`chan struct{}`) — pure exit signal
- Enforce migration timeouts regardless of job type — `processInflightMigration` runs every iteration even when `GetJobStats` fails or returns `JOB_NONE`

#### Reduce noisy abort logs
- `cancelMigration` returns nil and logs when migration is not active or abort already in progress/succeeded — eliminates error propagation through gRPC for expected conditions
- virt-handler `handleMigrationAbort` checks both VMI status and domain metadata before issuing cancel RPC — eliminates redundant calls
- Remove unused `CancelMigrationFailedVmiNotMigratingErr` constant

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The migration monitor accumulated overlapping error handling, redundant status-setting paths, and mixed abort/result responsibilities that made the code hard to reason about and caused observable issues:
- Stale domain sends racing with fresh metadata notifications
- Redundant abort RPC calls from virt-handler due to stale status and broken error string matching
- Timeouts not firing when `GetJobStats` fails or returns `JOB_NONE`

### Special notes for your reviewer

The commits are ordered to be individually reviewable. The abort decoupling series builds incrementally — each step preserves correctness while removing one mixed responsibility.

#### Before this PR:
When a guest agent becomes temporarily unavailable during maintenance operations (e.g., guest OS updates, Windows updates), the GuestAgentPing liveness probe fails and causes the Pod to restart. There is no way to temporarily suppress probe checks without removing the probe from the VMI spec entirely, which requires recreating the  VMI. 
#### After this PR:
Users can pause GuestAgentPing probes by setting the annotation host-215.example/pause-guest-agent-probes: "true" on a VMI. While the annotation is set, virt-launcher short-circuits GuestPing calls and returns immediate success without contacting the QEMU guest agent, preventing unnecessary Pod restarts during maintenance windows. Removing the annotation resumes normal probe behavior.

### What this PR does
In some test environments, hotplug LUN tests are seen failing during test cleanup when trying to remove the `scsi_debug` module because the block device is still seen in use. ```"failed executing command=[/usr/bin/virt-chroot --mount /proc/1/ns/mnt exec -- /usr/sbin/modprobe -r scsi_debug], error=command terminated with exit code 1, stdout=, stderr=modprobe: FATAL: Module scsi_debug is in use.\n",```

The test completes after it verifies the volume has been unplugged and the device is no longer accessible on the guest, it then proceeds to the cleanup step to remove the scsi module. However during this time, it is possible that the attachment pod is still in the process of being cleaned up and still has the block device bind mounted.

To avoid this potential conflict, this PR wraps this module removal logic in an Eventually retry to allow the pod enough time to be cleaned up to ensure the block device is no longer in use.

Fixes: https://host-696.example/browse/TICKET-337464

### What this PR does
#### Before this PR:

Proj lacks support for advanced ARM64 GPU passthrough (specifically NVIDIA Grace platforms), which requires SMMUv3 IOMMU, IOMMUFD, and specialized NUMA topologies

#### After this PR:

This is the first in a series of PRs to bring this capability into mainline Proj (ported from proj-aie#10). 
It establishes the foundational types and plumbing:

 - Introduces the GraceIOVirtualization feature gate (Alpha, off by default) and plumbs it through virt-handler to virt-launcher.
 - Adds libvirt domain XML schemas (IOMMUDevice, IOMMUDriver) to emit SMMUv3 devices.
 - Extends HostDevice with Driver (for IOMMUFD) and ACPI (for NUMA proximity domain) fields.
 - Modifies NUMACell.Memory to a pointer and makes CPUs omitempty to support zero-memory, CPU-less NUMA cells.

### References
- VEP tracking issue: https://host-623.example/proj/enhancements/issues/44920

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way
This ports the foundational architecture from the proj-aie fork upstream. 
By isolating the schema updates and feature-gate plumbing into this initial PR, we keep the diff easily reviewable and unblock the subsequent functionality and validation PRs.

### Special notes for your reviewer
 - This PR is purely additive. There are no behavioral changes unless the feature gate is explicitly enabled.
 - The NUMACell.Memory pointer change required updates to existing test fixtures, which are included here.

Next: Follow-up PRs will introduce IOMMU detection, the SMMUv3 converter, PCI isolation, PCIHole64 sizing, and webhook validation.

{"author": "person-25b5e478", "base": "main", "body": "### What this PR does
#### Before this PR:

The Plugin CRD exists (https://host-623.example/proj/proj/pull/96739) with structural validation via ValidatingAdmissionPolicies, but domain hooks have no evaluation engine.

#### After this PR:

Plugin domain hooks are fully functional. CEL expressions are validated at admission time, delivered to virt-launcher via protobuf, and evaluated during domain define to produce partial domain XML mutations.

### References

- VEP tracking issue: https://host-623.example/proj/enhancements/issues/32520
- Depends on https://host-623.example/proj/proj/pull/96739

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

Plugin domain hooks use CEL expressions that produce partial struct literals - e.g. `Domain{Devices: DomainDeviceList{Watchdogs: [DomainWatchdog{Model: "i6300esb"}]}}`. The challenge is that default CEL struct construction zero-fills every unmentioned field, making it impossible to distinguish "plugin set this to zero" from "plugin didn't set this field." A naive merge would overwrite the entire domain with zeros.

This is solved with a sparse value layer: a custom CEL provider overrides struct construction to return map-backed values that track only the fields a CEL expression explicitly sets. After evaluation, a deep merge walks the sparse result and applies only those fields onto a copy of the original domain. This lets plugins express surgical partial mutations naturally without needing to reproduce the entire domain.

{"author": "person-1afedb80", "base": "main", "body": "### What this PR does
Fix `ExpectResumingNodeLabellerToSucceed` timing out on ARM64 nodes in multi-arch clusters.

The function verifies the node-labeller has resumed by removing a label and waiting for it to reappear. It used `HostModelCPULabel` for this, but ARM64 nodes never produce host-model labels (`supportsHostModel` returns false), so the re-check always times out.

Switch to `SupportedMachineTypeLabel` which the node-labeller produces on all architectures unconditionally.

#### Before this PR:
- Uses `HostModelCPULabel` as the verification label — only produced on amd64/s390x
- ARM64 nodes time out waiting for a label that will never be applied

#### After this PR:
- Uses `SupportedMachineTypeLabel` as the verification label — produced on all architectures
- No arch-specific branching needed

### References
Part of: https://host-623.example/proj/proj/issues/80591

### Release note

NONE

{"author": "person-1afedb80", "base": "main", "body": "### What this PR does
Decorates test_id:6995 (TSC frequency and scalability) with `RequiresAMD64`. TSC labels are only populated on AMD64 nodes and this test will never apply to other architectures.

#### Before this PR:
- The test takes `nodesWithHypervisor[0]` which may be a non-AMD64 node, causing the test to fail on mixed-arch clusters

#### After this PR:
- The test is skipped on non-AMD64 clusters via `RequiresAMD64` and explicitly selects an AMD64 node from the hypervisor list

{"author": "person-1afedb80", "base": "main", "body": "### What this PR does
Fixes the migration abort test ("should be able to properly abort migration") failing on multi-arch clusters.

In `tests/component-539/migration.go`, the test's `BeforeEach` calls `GetAllSchedulableNodes()` and marks all nodes except the last one as unschedulable — before the VMI is created. The VMI is then created without an explicit architecture, so it defaults to the control plane's architecture (amd64). On a multi-arch cluster, the only remaining schedulable node may be ARM64. The VMI's pod gets `host-860.example/arch=amd64` in its nodeSelector (added by the mutating webhook), which conflicts with the ARM64 node — the VMI becomes Unschedulable and the test fails before it even reaches the migration logic.

The fix moves the node-unschedulable setup into the test body, after the VMI has started. The VMI schedules freely on any compatible node first, then all other schedulable nodes are marked unschedulable so the migration target cannot be placed — which is the actual test precondition.

#### Before this PR:
- `BeforeEach` marks all nodes except the last as unschedulable
- VMI is created without explicit architecture (defaults to amd64)
- On multi-arch clusters, the remaining node may be ARM64
- Pod gets `host-860.example/arch=amd64` nodeSelector → conflicts with the ARM64 node → Unschedulable

#### After this PR:
- VMI is created and schedules on any compatible node
- After VMI is running, all other nodes are marked unschedulable
- Migration attempt correctly gets stuck (no target node available)
- No architecture assumptions needed

Part of: https://host-623.example/proj/proj/issues/80591

### What this PR does
#### Before this PR:

IOMMUFD support for device passthrough required deploying the external [iommufd-device-plugin](https://host-623.example/proj/iommufd-device-plugin) DaemonSet separately from Proj.

#### After this PR:

The IOMMUFD device plugin is integrated directly into virt-handler's device manager behind a new `IOMMUFD` Alpha feature gate. When enabled, virt-handler manages the `devices.proj.example/iommufd` device plugin natively. The plugin opens `/dev/iommu`, configures `IOMMU_OPTION_RLIMIT_MODE` (replicating libvirt's `virIOMMUFDOpenDevice`), and passes the pre-configured FD to virt-launcher via `SCM_RIGHTS` over a Unix socket. It gracefully degrades on nodes without `/dev/iommu` by returning successful empty responses, so pods are never rejected due to missing IOMMUFD support.

### References
<!-- optional,
  Use `Fixes #<issue number>(, Fixes #<issue_number>, ...)` format, to close the issue(s) when PR gets merged.
  Use `Partially addresses #<issue number>` to link an issue without closing it when the PR merges.
  
- Fixes #
- Partially addresses #
-->
<!-- optional,
  VEP tracking issue if this PR is implementing one.
  For additional info about VEP tracking issue, see https://host-623.example/proj/enhancements#process
  
-->
- VEP tracking issue: https://host-623.example/proj/enhancements/issues/77991

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way
The following tradeoffs were made:
- The plugin is integrated into virt-handler rather than kept as an external DaemonSet to simplify deployment and lifecycle management ? one less component to deploy and maintain.
- SELinux relabeling is done inline via `lsetxattr` syscall rather than using the existing `selinux.SELinuxExecutor`, since the IOMMUFD plugin requires relabeling temporary device nodes (not just sockets), and the approach must work inside privileged containers where selinuxfs may not be mounted.

The following alternatives were considered:
- Keeping the external DaemonSet and only adding awareness of the resource in virt-handler. This was rejected because tight integration allows the plugin lifecycle to be managed by the existing device controller and gated behind a feature gate.

Links to places where the discussion took place: <!-- optional: slack, other GH issue, mailinglist, ... -->

### Special notes for your reviewer

<!-- optional -->

On kernels 6.2+, IOMMUFD supersedes the legacy VFIO container model. The temporary device node + SELinux relabeling approach is necessary because when an FD opened from `/dev/iommu` (context `device_t`) is passed via `SCM_RIGHTS`, the kernel's `security_file_receive()` check blocks `container_t` from receiving it. Creating a relabeled temporary char device with the same major/minor bypasses this.

{"author": "person-43208b11", "base": "main", "body": "### What this PR does
The install-strategy job is the one workload virt-operator creates outside the install strategy itself: it is generated on the fly and submitted directly, so it never passes through Customizer.Apply the way Deployments, DaemonSets and the other components do. As a result it could not be customized at all, and in particular there was no way to give its container resource requests and limits. On clusters that enforce an "every container must declare resources" admission policy this forced operators to exempt the whole Proj namespace or relax the policy during upgrades.

Run the customizer over the job before submitting it so that
customizeComponents.Patches with resourceType "Job" now apply to it.

#### Before this PR:
`customizeComponents.Patches` can't touch the install-strategy job. It's built ad-hoc and submitted directly, outside the targetStrategy path that `Customizer.Apply` iterates, so any patch targeting it is silently ignored. The job container has no resource requests/limits and no way to set them, so clusters that enforce a "containers must declare resources" admission policy have to either exempt the whole Proj namespace or disable the check during upgrades.

#### After this PR:
A patch with `resourceType: Job` and `resourceName: virt-operator-install-strategy` is applied to the install-strategy job before it's submitted.

### References
None — happy to file an issue if needed for tracking.

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way
`GenericApplyPatches` derives the match name from `ObjectMeta.Name`, which is empty for the install-strategy job since it uses `GenerateName`. So this does two things: falls back to `GenerateName` (minus the trailing `-`) when `Name` is unset, and gives the job a stable `GenerateName` so it's actually matchable.

The following tradeoffs were made:
- The job's `GenerateName` changes from `proj-<deploymentID>-job` to a stable `virt-operator-install-strategy-`. The old name embedded a SHA1 of the deployment config, so it changed on every version bump — making pinning a patch not possible. The job is correlated by the `host-215.example/install-strategy-identifier` annotation, not its name, and I couldn't find anything in-tree that keys on the old name pattern, so I believe this is safe. The one risk is an external consumer doing a prefix match on `proj-*-job` e.g. (log scraping, a Kyverno/OPA rule, a runbook). I think that's unlikely for an ephemeral operator-managed job, but it's a behavior change. The associated install-strategy ConfigMap already uses a stable `proj-install-strategy-` GenerateName.
- Reused the existing `customizeComponents.Patches` mechanism instead of adding a typed field. Costs the name change above, but you get full control of the job (resources, env, securityContext, ...) rather than just one field, and there's no new API surface.

The following alternatives were considered:
- A typed `spec.infra.resources` field on `ComponentConfig`. Rejected: it lives
  on the struct shared with `spec.workloads`, where it'd silently no-op, and the
  API shape (one field that only affects a single Job) doesn't match the
  behavior.
- A dedicated `spec.installStrategy` struct. Over-engineered for something only
  relevant during install/upgrade.
- Matching by the job's pod label (`virt-operator-strategy-dumper`) instead of its name, which would avoid the GenerateName change entirely. It needs a complex apply method rather than reusing `GenericApplyPatches`; I went with a name-based approach to keep it concise. 

### Special notes for your reviewer
- The `GenericApplyPatches` GenerateName fallback is generic — any `GenerateName`-only object now matches by its prefix, not just this job.
- Heads up on the `GenerateName` change described above in case you feel differently about the external-matcher risk.

{"author": "person-1afedb80", "base": "main", "body": "### What this PR does
Sets `Platform.Architecture` on DataVolume registry sources in migration tests using the cluster's default architecture (`kv.Status.DefaultArchitecture`) instead of reading a random node's arch via `nodes.Items[0]`.

When CDI imports a container disk image using `RegistryPullNode`, the importer pod can land on any node in the cluster. The node's container runtime pulls the image variant matching its own architecture. On a multi-arch cluster, if the importer lands on an ARM64 node, it pulls the ARM64 disk image into the shared PVC. The VMI then defaults to amd64 (set by the mutating webhook) and tries to boot the ARM64 disk — QEMU starts but the OS never boots, causing login timeouts.

The fix uses `kv.Status.DefaultArchitecture` — the same value the mutating webhook assigns to VMIs without an explicit architecture. Setting `Platform.Architecture` on the DataVolume to this value tells CDI to constrain the importer pod to nodes of the matching architecture, guaranteeing the imported disk matches what the VMI will boot. No `WithArchitecture` is needed on the VMIs themselves since the webhook already defaults them to this value.

#### Before this PR:
- DataVolumes with `RegistryPullNode` don't specify a platform architecture
- On multi-arch clusters, the importer pod can land on any node and pull the wrong architecture's disk image
- The VMI defaults to amd64 but may boot an ARM64 disk → login timeout

#### After this PR:
- All DataVolume registry sources specify `Platform.Architecture` from `kv.Status.DefaultArchitecture`
- CDI constrains the importer pod to nodes matching the cluster's default architecture
- The imported disk image is guaranteed to match the VMI's architecture
- Adds `GetDefaultArchitecture()` helper in `tests/component-667/`
- Adds composable `RegistryOption` functions (`RegistryWithPullMethod`, `RegistryWithPlatformArch`) in `pkg/component-136/`
- Refactors `WithRegistryURLSourceAndPullMethod` to compose from `WithRegistryURLSource` + options

{"author": "person-e18249dc", "base": "main", "body": "Add DiskSourcePathHook that updates disk source file paths in the
domain XML on the target virt-launcher pod by replacing the VMI
namespace segment with the target domain namespace.

Currently, disk source path adjustments happen on the migration
source side. This is problematic because during upgrades, only the
target pod runs the new virt-launcher image while the source pod
still runs the old one. If a bug fix is applied to this logic, it
will not take effect during rolling upgrades since the source pod
cannot be updated. Moving these modifications to the target side
ensures that fixes are always applied by the new code.

As part of VEP-141 Beta, all target-specific domain XML modifications
are being moved to target-side pre-migration hooks.

The source-side logic is kept (with a TODO to remove post-GA)
because it is still needed when the LibvirtHooksServerAndClient
feature gate is disabled.

### What this PR does
#### Before this PR:
QEMU marks discarded blocks as dirty in the checkpoint bitmap. Previously, the `Map()` endpoint queried only a single metadata context so these trimmed blocks appeared as regular dirty extents which caused incremental backups to transfer an additional amount of zeros.

#### After this PR:
This PR registers both `base:allocation` and `qemu:dirty-bitmap` contexts for incremental backups. It introduces `mergedContextMapper` which buffers both contexts' extents per `BlockStatus64` call, then merges them inline using a two-pointer walk with flag remapping (allocation hole/zero collapsed to bit 1, dirty stays on bit 0). The merged output distinguishes clean (0), dirty (1), zero (2), and dirty,zero (3).

Additionally extracted shared batching and coalescing logic into `extentBatcher`.

{"author": "person-1f060cd7", "base": "main", "body": "### What this PR does
When an optional feature gate (e.g. VirtTemplateDeployment) is enabled without a version/registry change, the infrastructureRolledOver check hits the fallback branch:

  (targetVersion == observedVersion) && (targetImageRegistry == observedImageRegistry)

This causes Sync() to return true (AllResourcesCreated) before the new feature's pods are ready. Previously, SetObservedDeploymentConfig was called immediately on synced=true, updating ObservedDeploymentID to the new value. On the next reconcile, isUpdating() returned false (Target == Observed), so UpdateConditionsDeploying was called, setting Available=False. The system was stuck in this "DeploymentInProgress" loop indefinitely because isReady() kept returning false while the new pods were starting.

Fix: move SetObservedDeploymentConfig inside the isReady() block. Now ObservedDeploymentID is only updated once ALL pods (including the newly enabled optional feature) are actually ready. During the transition:
  - isUpdating() returns true → UpdateConditionsUpdating → Available=True
  - When pods become ready → SetObservedDeploymentConfig called
  - isUpdating() becomes false → UpdateConditionsAvailable sets the final Available=True, Progressing=False state

- Fixes TICKET-512057

{"author": "person-d131fbd8", "base": "main", "body": "### What this PR does

#### Before this PR:

The linux-bridge ping tests in `vmi_multus.go` used a local `createVMIOnNode` helper that pinned both VMIs to `nodes.Items[0]` via
hard-coded node affinity. This approach is fragile: it selects a node by list index rather than by intent, and it bypassed the
`libvmi` option pattern by mutating `Spec.Domain.Devices.Interfaces` and `Spec.Networks` directly.

#### After this PR:

The two VMIs that must ping each other are co-located using **pod affinity**: each VMI carries a shared label and a
`RequiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` affinity term that matches it. Kubernetes scheduling ensures both land on the same
node without hard-coding any node name. A new `libvmi.WithRequiredPodAffinity` option (symmetric to the existing
`WithPreferredPodAffinity`) makes this reusable across the codebase.

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

Linux-bridge connectivity requires both VMIs to land on the same node — the bridge is node-local. The old implementation satisfied
this by pinning to `nodes.Items[0]`, which works but communicates the wrong intent: the constraint is *co-location*, not *a specific 
node*. Using pod affinity expresses the actual scheduling invariant and lets the scheduler pick any suitable node, improving
resilience in heterogeneous clusters.

The `withCoLocationAffinity(context)` helper applies both a label and the affinity term in one call, so the label used for matching is
guaranteed to be consistent. The `context` string namespaces distinct co-location groups within the same test run (e.g.
`"linux-bridge-ping"` vs `"linux-bridge-ipam"`).

`WithRequiredPodAffinity` was added to `pkg/component-607/selector.go` alongside `WithPreferredPodAffinity` to keep the affinity API
symmetric and discoverable.

### Special notes for your reviewer

The duplicate import alias `v13 "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/component-866/meta/v1"` (a leftover alias for `metav1`) is removed as a minor cleanup
made necessary by the refactor.

{"author": "person-1afedb80", "base": "main", "body": "### What this PR does
Removes the "should prevent scheduling of a pod for a VMI with an unsupported machine type" DescribeTable from `tests/component-124` (3 entries: amd64, arm64, s390x).

In this test, a VMI is created with an architecture-specific machine type (e.g. `virt-test-1.2.3` for arm64) but without setting `VMI.Spec.Architecture`. The mutating webhook resolves architecture to the cluster default (amd64). For the arm64 and s390x entries, the webhook then checks the machine type against the amd64 emulated machines list (`q35*`, `pc-q35*`) and rejects VMI creation because `virt-test-1.2.3` is not in that list.

Even if the architecture were set correctly, the core Proj logic being tested — adding `SupportedMachineTypeLabel` to the pod's nodeSelector — is already covered by the unit test in `pkg/component-919/services/template_test.go:1223` ("should add node selector for machine type"). The remainder of the e2e test only verifies that the k8s scheduler rejects a pod whose nodeSelector doesn't match any node, which is standard scheduler behavior.

#### Before this PR:
- Three e2e test entries create VMIs with architecture-specific machine types without setting architecture
- The arm64 and s390x entries fail on multi-arch clusters because the webhook resolves to amd64 and rejects the machine type

#### After this PR:
- The redundant e2e test is removed
- Machine-type nodeSelector logic remains covered by unit tests

{"author": "person-16a8f255", "base": "main", "body": "`setsched.go` is gated to `linux/{amd64,arm64,s390x}`. On every other GOOS/GOARCH the package leaves `SchedParam`, `SchedFIFO`, and `SchedSetScheduler` undefined, which breaks any transitive consumer, including some `pkg/component-264` tests.

- Extracted the shared types `SchedParam`, `policy`, `SchedFIFO` into a build-tag-neutral `setsched_common.go` so they are defined in exactly one place.
- Added a sibling `setsched_unsupported.go` with the inverse build tag that provides only the `SchedSetScheduler` stub, returning the sentinel `ErrUnsupportedRTScheduling` so a call cannot silently no-op on a platform without the syscall.

### What this PR does
#### Before this PR:
Cross-building `pkg/component-397/...` for any GOOS/GOARCH outside `linux/{amd64,arm64,s390x}` fails:
```
  pkg/component-397/kvm/realtime.go: undefined: common.SchedParam
  pkg/component-397/kvm/realtime.go: undefined: common.SchedSetScheduler
  pkg/component-397/kvm/realtime.go: undefined: common.SchedFIFO
  pkg/component-397/mshv/realtime.go: undefined: common.SchedParam
  ...
```
Anything transitively importing `pkg/component-397` fails the same way, which is how the reporter hit it when packaging `virtctl` for Alpine across `armhf`, `armv7`, `loongarch64`, `ppc64le`, `riscv64`, and `x86`.

#### After this PR:
`pkg/component-397/...` builds on every GOOS/GOARCH. Shared types `SchedParam`, `policy`, `SchedFIFO` live in build-tag-neutral `setsched_common.go`, so the real implementation in `setsched.go` and the stub in `setsched_unsupported.go` cannot drift. The stub returns the sentinel `ErrUnsupportedRTScheduling` for `errors.Is` checks.

### References
- Fixes #45133

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way
The following tradeoffs were made:
- The stub keeps the public surface defined on architectures where the underlying syscall is not available, in exchange for an explicit runtime error if anyone ever calls into it on those targets. Downstream packagers (Alpine and similar distros that ship `virtctl` across many arches) get a buildable package without Proj needing to claim runtime support on those arches.
  
The following alternatives were considered:
- Add matching `//go:build` constraints to each file in `pkg/component-397/kvm` and `pkg/component-397/mshv` that uses these symbols. Propagates the constraint up to every caller and leaves `pkg/component-397/launcherhypervisorresources.go` needing its own constraints. Larger blast radius for the same outcome.
- Move the symbols into `pkg/component-397/kvm` and `pkg/component-397/mshv` directly. Duplicates the same three definitions
in two places.
- The chosen approach localises the constraint to `pkg/component-397/common`, mirroring the existing `setsched.go` gate.

Verified locally with `go build ./pkg/component-397/...` across the matrix:
- Previously failing, now OK: `linux/riscv64`, `linux/ppc64le`, `linux/386`, `linux/arm`, `linux/loong64`
- No regression on supported targets: `linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`, `linux/s390x`

This violated the k8s API conventions that conditions should be observations of current state, not imperative control signals (https://host-623.example/kubernetes/community/blob/main/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#typical-status-properties).

#### After this PR:
The controller now derives its next action from either external resource state (e.g., VMI, VMExport) or its own status that isn't a condition (e.g., newly introduced `ExportUID`, `deletionTimestamp`). Conditions become a pure observation layer for users and tooling, collapsed to `Progressing` with reason variants and splitting the ambiguous `Done` into `Complete` and `Failed` similarly to a k8s job. Backup RPCs being idempotent allow the controller to re-send on every reconcile without needing edge-triggered guards.

{"author": "person-0c90002e", "base": "main", "body": "## What this PR does

### Before this PR

When multiple hotplug attachment pods co-exist, and these pods have volumes mounted from the same underlying block device, `parentMountInfoFor()` could select the wrong parent mount on the node.

This could result in intermittent mount/unmount cleanup failures and repeated VMI sync retries.

Additionally, `mountFromPod()` reused the same `sourceUID` variable while iterating over hotplug `VolumeStatus` entries. If one volume populated `sourceUID`, later volumes in the same sync loop could accidentally reuse that UID instead of their own `AttachPodUID`.

### After this PR

Mount resolution now uses pod UID-based disambiguation for kubelet pod mount paths:

`/var/lib/kubelet/pods/<POD_UID>/volumes/...`

This lets virt-handler select the mount belonging to the specific attachment pod it is operating on when multiple attachment pods exist simultaneously.

The pod UID filter is applied only to mountpoints under the configured kubelet pods directory, and it matches the pod UID as a full path segment. Mounts outside that directory, such as hostPath-backed parent mounts, keep the existing behavior.

This PR also scopes `sourceUID` per volume in `mountFromPod()`. If a later volume has no `AttachPodUID` yet, virt-handler skips mounting it until status is updated instead of reusing a stale UID from a previous volume.

## References

- Fixes: https://host-623.example/proj/proj/issues/61982
- Related PR: https://host-623.example/proj/proj/pull/45002
- Related issues:
  - https://host-623.example/proj/proj/issues/30384
  - https://host-623.example/proj/proj/issues/96687

## Why we need it and why it was done in this way

Hotplug volumes can share the same mount root on the node. During attach/detach operations, multiple hotplug attachment pods may briefly coexist, and a given volume can be attached to multiple pods concurrently.

Matching only by major/minor and mount root is not enough to disambiguate these mounts. Passing the attachment pod UID through the existing mount resolution path gives virt-handler the context it needs without adding API calls or changing stored data.

The per-volume `sourceUID` change keeps virt-handler aligned with the VMI status model: each hotplug volume status owns its own `AttachPodUID`.

## Special notes for your reviewer

- The pod UID filter is backward-compatible: an empty pod UID keeps the previous behavior.
- The filter only rejects mismatched kubelet pod mount paths, preserving hostPath-backed volume behavior.
- `MountFromPod(vmi, explicitUID, ...)` still uses the explicit UID for all volumes, which is needed for migration paths.
- Normal `Mount(vmi, ...)` now resolves the UID independently for each hotplug `VolumeStatus`.

{"author": "person-bf91c6e0", "base": "main", "body": "### What this PR does
#### Before this PR:
PRs that change RPM dependencies (WORKSPACE, rpm/BUILD.bazel, sandbox_hash) fail all CI lanes with:
```
ERROR: OCI Image //images/disks-images-provider:disks-images-provider-image failed:
Failed to fetch blobs because they do not exist remotely.
```
The `--remote_download_toplevel` flag prevents Bazel from downloading transitive action outputs (RPM tars, OCI layer blobs) locally. When combined with `bazel clean` during sandbox regeneration, the oci_image actions can't find their input blobs from either local disk or remote cache.

#### After this PR:
When a PR touches `rpm/` or `WORKSPACE` files, `automation/test.sh` detects the change and switches from `--remote_download_toplevel` to `--remote_download_all`. This ensures transitive inputs (RPM tars, base image layers) are downloaded locally so `oci_image` actions can find their inputs.

Non-RPM PRs continue to use `--remote_download_toplevel` for bandwidth savings — no change in behavior for the vast majority of CI runs.

#### Net effect on CI
- **RPM-bump PRs**: switch to `--remote_download_all`, downloading all intermediate action outputs. Moderate increase in build time and network I/O for these runs. Fixes the hard build failure.
- **All other PRs**: no change — continue using `--remote_download_toplevel` with the same performance characteristics as today.

#### Workaround for contributors
Until this fix is merged, contributors who need to land RPM-bump PRs can work around the issue by manually adding to `automation/test.sh`'s ci.bazelrc heredoc:
```bash
build --remote_download_all
```
Alternatively, ask a maintainer to `/override` the affected lanes if the Go build and link steps succeed.

### References
- Partially addresses #91494 — unblocks the libvirt/qemu bump PR which has been stuck on this failure across all k8s-1.36 lanes

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

**Root cause:** When a PR changes RPMs, the sandbox is regenerated and `bazel clean` runs, wiping all local state. The new RPM inputs produce novel action hashes. With `--remote_download_toplevel`, transitive outputs (like `//rpm:testimage_x86_64` tar layers feeding into `//images:proj-testing-base`) are not downloaded locally. For novel hashes, they don't exist in the remote cache either. The `oci_image` action can't get its input blobs from either source — a hard failure that retries cannot fix.

**Why conditional, not unconditional removal?** `--remote_download_toplevel` provides real bandwidth savings for the ~99% of PRs that don't touch RPMs. The conditional approach preserves those savings while fixing the structural failure for RPM-bump PRs.

**Why not a targeted fix (adding explicit top-level targets)?** The OCI image targets are already listed as explicit top-level targets in `hack/bazel-build-images.sh`. The problem is their **transitive** dependency chain (RPM tars → base image layers), which `--remote_download_toplevel` does not download regardless of what's listed as top-level.

**Detection mechanism:** Piggybacks on the existing `git diff --name-only` in `automation/test.sh` (line 37) that already computes `CI_GIT_ALL_CHANGES`. Files matching `^(rpm/|WORKSPACE)` trigger the fallback. For periodic/batch jobs where `PULL_BASE_SHA`/`PULL_PULL_SHA` are unset, `RPM_CHANGES` stays empty and `--remote_download_toplevel` is used — correct because periodics run against HEAD where the cache is warm.

**Evidence this is PR-specific, not infra-wide:**
| PR | Changes WORKSPACE/RPMs? | k8s-1.36 result |
|---|---|---|
| #50101 (1 test file) | No | All 6 lanes pass |
| #42433 (Go files only) | No | Build succeeds |
| #91494 (RPM bump) | Yes | All 6 lanes fail at OCI build |

- The explicit top-level target listing in `hack/bazel-build-functests.sh` (originally a workaround for `--remote_download_toplevel`) is left in place as it's harmless
- Only `automation/test.sh` is changed

{"author": "person-4c34b631", "base": "main", "body": "Fixes a race condition in `processVmDelete` where a stale launcher client
cache entry survives VMI teardown and poisons the next migration's
target controller, causing it to fail with
"Can not update a VirtualMachineInstance with unresponsive command server."

## Observed failure
[job-9083 #2011266924782652570](https://host-586.example/view/gs/proj-prow/pr-logs/pull/proj_proj/58273/job-9083/2011266924782652570)
Test `[test_id:93414] should be successfully migrated multiple times` —
Migration 0 completes, Migration 1 never starts. The target pod is
created but the source never begins sending data.


## Root cause
During Migration 0 teardown on the source node, the workqueue
re-enqueues the VMI key (triggered by the domain deletion event).
The second `processVmDelete` call runs `GetVerifiedLauncherClient`,
which discovers the still-lingering socket from the dying
virt-launcher pod and dials it successfully, re-creating a
`LauncherClientInfo` entry with `Ready=true`. The subsequent
`DeleteDomain` RPC fails with `codes.Unavailable` (connection refused
to the now-gone process). Because `IsDisconnected` does not recognize
`codes.Unavailable`, `processVmDelete` returns an error, which skips
`processVmCleanup` — the only place that clears the cache entry.
On the next reconcile, `isVMIOwnedByNode` returns false (the VMI has
moved), so the vm controller stops processing and the poisoned cache
entry becomes permanent. When Migration 1's target controller later
calls `GetLauncherClient`, it gets the stale entry, detects the socket
is gone, and enters the "unresponsive command server" error loop.
## Fix
Defer `CloseLauncherClient` at the top of `processVmDelete` so the
cache entry is always cleared regardless of how the function exits.
This matches the pattern already used in `MigrationTargetController.finalCleanup`
(added in PR #53604).

### Special notes for your reviewer

The 3rd commit removes the dependency on `vmi.Status.MigrationState.TargetCPUSet` and `vmi.Status.MigrationState.TargetNodeTopology` in the CPU dedicated hook.

These fields aren't available to the target-side hook because in `sync()`, `processVMI()` (which starts the hook server) runs before `updateStatus() `(which sets these fields). Previously, `processVMI()` ran on every reconcile, so on the second reconcile it would call `SyncMigrationTarget` again with the updated VMI. [This early return](https://host-623.example/proj/proj/blob/main/pkg/component-261/migration-target.go#L771-L774), introduced in PR #58315, prevents `processVMI` from running a second time, so the hook server never receives the updated VMI with those fields populated.

Instead of adding VMI status synchronization to restore the previous behavior, this commit reads the CPU set and topology directly from the `ConverterContext`, which is generated locally on the target pod. This is aligned with the expected deprecation of these fields as part of VEP-141 post-GA requirements and leads to a cleaner solution.

### What this PR does
PVC-based volumes (VolumeSource.PVC instead of VolumeSource.DataVolume)
were not checked for existence or CSI support before
migration, allowing incomplete MigratedVolumes entries to be written
which silently broke the migration flow. The migration target would get
`<disk type="file">` instead of `<disk type="block">` in the domain XML.

Add existence and CSI/volume-populator validation for PVC source
volumes, matching the existing DataVolume validation behavior.

was terminating. Several early-return paths also left stale addresses in
place.

Clear addresses when the lease-holder pod is terminating or unavailable.
Gate test fixture readiness on non-empty addresses when decentralized
live migration is enabled.
